author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: The Institutional Will: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: An institutional will is a coordinated set of decisions about authority, access, assets, archives, obligations, interpretation, privacy, and care—not a substitute for legal estate or corporate instruments.
frames.alt: Title plate for The Institutional Will.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: An accession-quality record preserves a house object beyond the founder’s lifetime while keeping the object, maker attribution, and museum stewardship distinct.
frames.credit: Gift of James A. and Mary Elizabeth Kingsland, 1994
frames.alt: Elaborate House of Worth silk fancy dress costume with a fitted bodice, dark patterned skirt, and dramatic decorative sleeves, around 1893.
frames.treatment: local display and download with attached credit

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · INTENT — What should happen—and why?. Write desired outcomes for company, name, work in progress, archive, public voice, teaching, licensing, philanthropy, privacy, dependents, and closure in plain language.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what should happen—and why? within The Institutional Will.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · AUTHORITY — Which instrument can make it happen?. Map corporate documents, contracts, employment terms, IP records, wills or trusts, powers, beneficiary designations, data policies, archive agreements, and jurisdiction-specific requirements with counsel.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping which instrument can make it happen? within The Institutional Will.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · STEWARD — Who acts, who substitutes, who reviews?. Name primary and alternate decision-makers by function; address conflicts, expertise, compensation, access, accountability, dissent, cultural authority, and removal.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who acts, who substitutes, who reviews? within The Institutional Will.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · REHEARSE — Does the plan work in practice?. Run incapacity, death, departure, sale, closure, dispute, data loss, platform failure, preservation emergency, and public controversy; record fixes and review dates.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping does the plan work in practice? within The Institutional Will.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: Founder intent can support clarity or attempt to control culture indefinitely. Successors, workers, collaborators, families, communities, law, and changing conditions retain claims and agency. A responsible plan governs interpretation rather than freezing it.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for The Institutional Will.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery
